articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches a mind-melting 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the delightfully named 'BlueHammer' weakness in Windows Defender. When your security software needs security patches, you know we're living in the matrix.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence is mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens by exploiting ancient router vulnerabilities. Because why break into one system when you can pwn the entire authentication infrastructure?

articles.title: Milestone 1.0.0 Release of APK Downloader `apkeep` Powers Research on Android Apps
articles.summary: Germany finally unmasked 'UNKN,' the mysterious Russian puppet master behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware empires. Daniil Shchukin's 15 minutes of fame comes with a side of computer sabotage charges.

articles.title: Yet Another Way to Bypass Google Chrome's Encryption Protection
articles.summary: NSA whistleblower William Binney reminds us about the 'turnkey totalitarian state' — because apparently we needed another reason to lose sleep over surveillance capitalism. The empire strikes back, indeed.

articles.title: From Stuxnet to ChatGPT: 20 News Events That Shaped Cyber
articles.summary: ShinyHunters breached Instructure's Canvas LMS, exposing how educational institutions basically hand over the keys to the kingdom to their vendors. Trust but verify, schools — emphasis on verify.

articles.title: India orders infosec red alert in case Mythos sparks crime spree
articles.summary: UK's age-gating plans could literally break the internet, privacy groups warn. Because nothing says 'child safety' like destroying fundamental web architecture and creating a surveillance dystopia.

articles.title: Mirai-Based xlabs_v1 Botnet Exploits ADB to Hijack IoT Devices for DDoS Attacks
articles.summary: A dozen critical vulnerabilities in vm2 Node.js library let attackers escape sandboxes and execute arbitrary code. When your security sandbox becomes a playground for hackers, it's time to rethink containment strategies.

articles.title: The Hacker News Launches 'Cybersecurity Stars Awards 2026' — Submissions Now Open
articles.summary: Iran's MuddyWater crew used Microsoft Teams for credential theft in a false flag ransomware op. Because apparently even state-sponsored hackers have embraced remote collaboration tools.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: AI-Powered Phishing, Android Spying Tool, Linux Exploit, GitHub RCE & More
articles.summary: Instructure hacker claims to have stolen 280 million records from 8,800 educational institutions. That's not a data breach — that's a full-scale educational apocalypse with a side of identity theft.

articles.title: Should You Be Worried About Copy Fail Linux Exploitation?
articles.summary: 2026 declared the year of AI-assisted attacks after a 17-year-old in Japan extracted 7 million user records from internet cafes. The kids are not alright — they're weaponizing artificial intelligence.
